items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: He said, “let me worry about that.” He said, “your eyes will catch up to your hands, don’t worry.”

ctx.x: No Joe was gone by then. But the drummer that I did see there was Jake Hanna. And that was my first meeting with Jake. But let’s see, okay, so anyway, let’s get back to when I was 15, during that summer break, I had played with the band, okay, in the fall, at age 15 I had been released from my medical restrictions because of the mononucleosis, to go back to school. The phone rings and now they want me to play at Memory Lane with the Salt City Six. And now this job went on, they used to go from nine to one or nine…

year. That was between my junior and senior year. And I played with the high school band all of that time. I had actually, to back it up a little bit, from Parker School up the street, for disciplinary reasons, I was sent to St. Mary’s School which is right about seven houses that way. They didn’t have a band. So they figured — so here I am not really learning how to read music as well as I’d like to have, and Burton Stanley was a professor up at Potsdam, was the band director there.
